current_flow: Today: a clarification_needed response renders clarify.prompt and clarify.options as buttons (ask-panel.tsx:131-141); clicking one calls onAsk with either the bare option or '<question> (<option>)' when resumesQuestion, which goes back through the selector. periodChoice and periodControl now arrive from task 1 and NOTHING renders them. use-ask.run (use-ask.ts:60) trims the question, refuses a second request while isPending, holds ONE AbortController and ONE phase stream, and appends every result as a new turn; AskTurn is {question, response} with no id. api.ask already accepts {question, selection} and chat.service.ts runs such a request verbatim with zero selector calls.
summary: Cold read of the ask-period-continuation contract. Five findings, three of them decided by the human. The sharpest was self-inflicted: the contract demanded a 'verbatim' question while use-ask.ts:61 trims every send, so the exact-body leaf would have passed while the audit record stayed wrong. The read also showed that 'the rest of the thread stays interactive' could not be delivered by adding fields to AskTurn - it would have meant rewriting cancellation and phase ownership and regressing the abort test - and that the contract said the continuation retains the 'previous answer' when the turn being replaced is a clarification with no answer, wording carried over from task 3.
gaps: The contract demanded the question reach the request 'verbatim' while use-ask.ts:61 trims every question before sending, so the exact-body leaf as specified would have passed while the audit record was still being corrupted with a question the user did not ask.

'The rest of the thread stays interactive' could not be met by adding fields to AskTurn: ask-panel.tsx:66 disables suggestions and the composer from the GLOBAL isPending and use-ask.ts:62 rejects all concurrent work, so honouring it meant per-request controllers and per-turn phase ownership - which would regress the abort behaviour proven at ask-panel.test.tsx:450.

The contract never defined the target's identity: AskTurn (use-ask.ts:7) is {question, response} with no id, so two identical questions are indistinguishable and targeting by question or index is unsafe.

The contract said the continuation 'retains the previous answer', but the turn being replaced is a CLARIFICATION and has no answer - the author's own wording carried over from task 3. Without a rule, a failed period choice strands the user with the buttons gone and no retry.
'Any ResponseClass the server returns' was ambiguous: AskResponse also covers informational and clarification classes, so it did not say what actually replaces the turn.

The session's AskUserQuestion rounds were being ledgered into a DIFFERENT repo: .factory/ceremony-target pointed at /Users/caw-dev-m4-5/code/3oilpalm-multi-plant, so this story's human provenance landed against multi-plant and one of multi-plant's rounds appeared in this ledger. The pointer had been left untracked by another session and this session committed it into master in e73e07c via a blanket 'git add -A'.
resolutions: A dedicated criterion now requires the question to arrive BYTE-IDENTICAL and requires the exact-body leaf to use a periodChoice.question carrying leading and trailing whitespace, so the leaf fails while the trim is still there. The contract names use-ask.ts:61 as the cause.

HUMAN ROUND 1: concurrency is deliberately UNCHANGED. The single-in-flight rule and the global isPending lock stay; per-turn pending is presentation only. The contract states this as scope protection and names ask-panel.test.tsx:450 as the behaviour that must still pass unchanged, so an implementer cannot read 'per-turn' as a licence to rewrite cancellation.
A criterion now requires a STABLE TURN ID and targeting by it, citing AskTurn's lack of identity.

HUMAN ROUND 2: a failed click is never a dead end. The prompt and period buttons stay in that turn, re-enabled, with one plain failure line beneath, so the user can pick again or retry. The contract opens by CORRECTING its own 'previous answer' wording: what survives is the clarification, not an answer.

HUMAN ROUND 3: only a success response replaces the clarification. Every other typed response - another clarification, informational, blocked, not-supported - and every transport failure is that turn's failure with the buttons intact; an AbortError clears pending and is not shown as a failure. A clicked period returning a glossary definition is a failed click however well-typed it is.

Cleared with 'forge ceremony target clear' and the three rounds re-asked so they ledger against ask-period-control. The removal is committed so master stops carrying the pointer. Flagged to the human, because it silently affected a shared repo and would have kept misfiling every later round.

rounds.question: Re-asking only because a stale pointer filed your last answers into another repo. While a clicked period is being fetched, should the rest of Ask stay usable?
options: Lock the panel while it runs (Recommended)
Allow a new ask alongside it
rounds.chosen: Lock the panel while it runs (Recommended)

rounds.question: If a clicked period fails (server refuses it, or the network drops), what should the user be left looking at?
A clicked period can come back as something other than a data answer — another clarification, or an informational glossary reply. Which should take over the turn?

criteria_map.A clarification_needed response carrying: Rendering the choice. Verified ask-panel.tsx:131-141 renders clarify.options today and that the two payloads must be distinguished by which field is present.
criteria_map.Clicking an option posts AskRequest.sele: Continue with data. The measured 2/4 and 3/4 word-append figures are why; the criterion pins the request body rather than the outcome.
criteria_map.The question reaches the request BYTE-ID: Byte-identical question. Added because the cold read found use-ask.ts:61 trims - the original 'verbatim' wording was unfalsifiable as written.
criteria_map.A turn gains a STABLE ID and the continu: Stable turn id. Added because AskTurn has no identity and duplicate questions make index targeting unsafe.
criteria_map.ONLY a success response replaces the cla: Only success replaces. Human round 3; the alternative would let a clicked period degrade to a definition, which is the failure this story exists to remove.
criteria_map.Concurrency is UNCHANGED: use-ask.ts:62: Concurrency unchanged. Human round 1; scope protection with the regression test named so it cannot be read as a licence to rewrite cancellation.
criteria_map.Frontend leaves cover: rendering a perio: The leaf matrix, judged by testcase NAME after the junit false-green lesson.
criteria_map.user_facing: true. emil-design-eng and f: Design skills, mandatory for a user_facing task, with the 360px docked width called out because the panel has two widths.

new_abstractions: A stable turn identity in use-ask, which the thread has never had; it is what makes a targeted replacement safe when two questions are identical.
A continuation path that posts a SELECTION rather than a question, the first client use of AskRequest.selection.
Per-turn presentation state (pending and failure attached to a turn) held alongside, and deliberately not replacing, the panel's single-in-flight lock.
